Base release written just 'Vintage'/'Dom Perignon Vintage 2008' - 'P1' is informal critic shorthand, never real printed wording (domperignon.com itself blocked by an age-gate; base-release wording confirmed via multi-merchant corroboration instead). P2/P3 real titles vary in word order: 'Dom Perignon P2 2002' (Hedonism), '2002 Dom Perignon, P2' (Jeroboams), 'Dom Perignon Brut, P2 Vintage' (HDH Wine), 'Dom Perignon P2 Vintage 2002' (Bodeboca). 'P2'/'Plenitude 2' always co-occurs with the 4-digit vintage year; word order is not fixed. House replaced an older 'Oenotheque' designation with P2/P3 around 2014-2016 per Decanter. Same wine, same vintage, different market release - treat P2/P3 as a release_code on this one cuvee, exactly like a Krug edition, never a separate cuvee row.
